title: Breaking: Galaxy S26 series gets seventh One UI 9 beta release with new AI features
summary: Samsung hasn't mentioned which new features, but they could be the AI features from the Galaxy Z Fold 8.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has released the seventh One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. The 1,234MB update (firmware ZZHK) includes the August 5, 2026, security patch and introduces new AI features, though Samsung hasn’t detailed which ones. Currently live in Germany, India, Poland, the UK, and South Korea, the new update will soon be available in the US as well. Earlier this week, Samsung released One UI 9 Beta 6 for the Galaxy S26 series . Samsung usually goes a few weeks between beta releases, and while we hoped for a stable update to finally roll out, there were indications that Samsung was working on yet another beta update . Turns out it was, as Samsung has begun rolling out One UI 9 Beta 7 for the Galaxy S26 series. We’ve received the seventh One UI 9 update on our Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK. This Android 17-based update comes with firmware version ending in ZZHK, the August 5, 2026 security patch, and is 1,234MB in size.

title: This repairable Android phone just won over almost everyone
summary: On its US release, we ran a poll asking whether you liked the new Fairphone Gen 6 Plus. You gave us a resounding answer.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority The Samsung Galaxy S5 still has a special place in my heart, purely because I could pop the back off and swap in a fresh battery myself. Phones have come a long way since then, and that kind of easy repairability largely disappeared along the way. But Fairphone has spent years trying to keep the idea alive, and its latest phone brings that philosophy to the US more directly than ever. The Fairphone Gen 6 Plus is the first model the company is selling directly in the US — rather than through Murena — and it runs the standard Google-equipped version of Android. It costs $649 and lets you replace up to 12 components with a single screwdriver, including the battery, display, cameras, and USB-C port. The upgrades over the regular Gen 6 are fairly modest, but we still wanted to know what you made of the package. We asked our readers whether the Gen 6 Plus was hot in a recent poll, and the results could hardly have been more definitive. Take a look for yourself.

Microduck comes with learned behaviors and can be controlled with a gamepad, but developers can also teach it new skills through reinforcement learning, simulation, and open-source software. AI has earned an overwhelmingly negative perception over the last couple of years. At this point, is there any way for the technology to shed that stigma and become more approachable to the general public? One of the best attempts at that may be Hugging Face’s new tiny duck-like robot. Hugging Face has unveiled a cute bipedal robot known as Microduck. The robot is about 10 inches tall and features 15 motors, a camera, a depth sensor, two inertial measurement units (IMU), and an articulated beak that can pick up objects. According to the company, the duck character was born as a result of the robot’s proportions, beak, and waddling gait.

body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Google killed support for 32-bit apps in Android a few years ago, but it turns out there is a solution. VPhoneOS is an app that lets you run 32-bit apps on new Android phones. This means you can play a ton of abandoned games on your Android device. One of the most disappointing changes to Android in recent years has been the decision to drop support for 32-bit apps. This won’t affect the vast majority of people, but I found it particularly unfortunate due to the wide variety of abandoned classic Android games . Fortunately, a solution has been flying under the radar for a while if you want to run classic Android games on your new phone. I recently stumbled across the VPhoneOS app, and it’s actually been available for a couple of years now. Simply put, VPhoneOS lets you install and run 32-bit apps on your Android device. VPhoneOS supports 32-bit Android apps via a virtual machine. Free users can run a virtual machine based on Android 7, while VIP subscribers get access to Android 10 and Android 12, along with 64-bit app support.
